title: Micro token ramp for dense controls and chart overlays
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: define a compact, micro-scale token ramp and a pragmatic migration strategy for dense controls (table rows, compact action bars, inline form fields) and chart overlays. Scope covers color palette deltas for high-density surfaces, condensed typography steps for small-footprint components, refined spacing/radius scales for 8px->4px micro gutters, and a lightweight elevation/shadow regimen tuned for stacked chart layers and dense lists.

Motivation: customers building analytics and admin UIs repeatedly ask for a higher-density option that preserves legibility and accessibility while reducing per-row height and visual clutter. Current token set is tuned for medium density and produces excessive vertical rhythm in compact tables and chart legends. This ticket aims to produce a small, well-documented token subset (micro-ramp) with clear migration guidance and automated codemods where possible.

Design constraints & trade-offs:
- Accessibility: maintain WCAG contrast >= 4.5:1 for primary text at small sizes where feasible; for secondary labels consider 3:1 with explicit guidance.
- Density vs touch targets: for mobile contexts we will not apply micro tokens; recommendation will be desktop-only for components with mouse/keyboard primary input.
- Performance: prefer CSS variable-based tokens for runtime theming; avoid excessive runtime calculations in the console that harm paint cost.
- Theming & palette complexity: introduce 4 compact semantic ramps (surface, muted, accent, interactive) derived from existing palette to avoid fragmenting color maintenance.

Deliverables:
1) Token spec document (colors, type scale, spacing, radii, elevation) with examples for tables, buttons, and charts.
2) Figma component variants and annotated tokens.
3) SCSS/CSS variable token file and migration codemod for core components.
4) Accessibility guidelines and QA checklist including contrast test vectors and example screen reader notes.
5) Rollout plan: opt-in feature flag in Console, telemetry to monitor adoption and any regression in error/issue rates.

Acceptance criteria:
- Compact tokens render consistent across Chrome/Firefox/Safari at desktop widths.
- Table row height reduced by >= 18% without losing readability for 12px/13px body text following contrast guidance.
- Chart overlays (legends, annotations) use tokenized shadows/elevation to maintain layer separation at reduced spacing.
- Codemod converts 80% of internal usages in main repo with no visual regressions flagged by visual diff.
- Documentation published on design system site with example PRs and migration checklist.
